title: 'The problem and the solution': Netanyahu-Sharaa call exposes Israel's Syria dilemma
gist: Netanyahu disclosed a July 2025 call with Syrian President al-Sharaa that he says stopped the Suwayda massacre, but Israel-Syria security talks have stalled since March and Israel still distrusts Damascus.

insights.claim: Netanyahu revealed he spoke with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in July 2025, the first publicly disclosed contact between the two countries' leaders.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Confirms a direct leader channel despite hostile public posture.

insights.claim: Israel-Syria negotiations on security arrangements have stalled since March, after the US and Israel launched their attack on Iran.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: The Iran war froze Israel-Syria de-escalation; a security deal is unlikely near term.

insights.claim: Despite Syrian efforts to curb arms smuggling to Hezbollah in Lebanon, Israel continues to view Damascus with suspicion, according to Israeli diplomatic sources.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Israeli mistrust sustains military posture in southern Syria.

insights.claim: Netanyahu said the call was prompted by violence between Druze and Bedouin groups around Suwayda last summer, in which more than 1,700 people were killed and some government forces sided with Bedouin fighters.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Israel positions itself as protector of Syria's Druze, justifying involvement.
insights.quote: I called Sharaa. It was a very brief and to-the-point conversation, and the massacre stopped

insights.claim: Haaretz reported, citing Syrian diplomatic sources, that the conversation also included a US representative and an official from another Arab country.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Suggests a multilateral mediation format rather than a bilateral channel.
